mainTopic: Why גוים are suspected of bestiality, and when that suspicion applies
overview: Our משנה says we may not leave an animal alone with a גוי, because גוים are suspected of bestiality. The גמרא asks why a ברייתא lets us buy animals from גוים for a קרבן without this worry. רב answers that a גוי protects his own animal so it will not become barren, and רב כהנא adds that with males it weakens their flesh. A גוי shepherd also holds back, because he fears losing his wages. That fear only works when the owner is another גוי who could catch him, so we may not hand our animal to a גוי shepherd. The גמרא then discusses gentile women: an animal following her around would expose her, but a dog would not, which is why a widow should not raise a dog. Next it explains why even female animals may not be left with gentile women, and traces the desire back to the זוהמא the נחש put into חוה, which ended for ישראל at הר סיני. Finally, two eyewitness stories show that the worry includes birds too.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to contradict the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lets us buy animals from גוים for a קרבן with no worry about bestiality or idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The גמרא raises a contradiction: We may buy an animal from גוים for a קרבן. We do not worry that it is a רובע, a נרבע, a מוקצה, or a נעבד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to set up a contradiction with our משנה. The next step will spell out exactly where the clash is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה assumes a גוי might commit bestiality with an animal. But this ברייתא says we may buy an animal from a גוי for a קרבן without worrying about that at all. Each of these four problems would make an animal unfit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction; it brings a source that seems to clash with what we just learned
An animal that did a sexual act with a person
An animal that a person did a sexual act with
An animal set aside to be offered to an idol
An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The contradiction is with our משנה, which says גוים are suspected of bestiality with animals.

phrases.english: We may buy an animal from them for an offering,
and we are not concerned, not because of an animal that mounted a person,
and not because of an animal that was mounted,
and not because of one set aside,
and not because of one that was worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by contrasting the משנה with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption that גוים are suspected of bestiality.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If גוים are suspected, a ברייתא should not allow buying their animals for a קרבן with no worry.

steps.title: Idol worship is understandable, but bestiality should still worry us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why מוקצה and נעבד are not a worry, then presses that רובע and נרבע should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that we do not worry about מוקצה and נעבד. If the גוי had set the animal aside for his idol or worshipped it, he would not have sold it. But רובע and נרבע should still worry us!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sorts the four worries in the ברייתא. Two of them are easy to explain, and the other two are the real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי would not sell an animal he dedicated to his idol or worshipped, so the sale itself shows it is not מוקצה or נעבד. Selling the animal proves nothing about bestiality, though. So according to our משנה, we should still worry about רובע and נרבע.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted; it sets up an easy case before the hard one
He set it aside (for idol worship)

phrases.english: It makes sense regarding one set aside and one worshipped,
because if it were so that he had set it aside
or if it were so that he had worshipped it —
he would not have sold it,
but for one that mounted and one that was mounted, let us be concerned!
phrases.notes: Our משנה says we should worry about bestiality, so the ברייתא seems to go against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the contradiction from step 1 to רובע and נרבע.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that we do not worry about רובע and נרבע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sale explains away idol worship but not bestiality, so the משנה's suspicion should apply.

steps.title: A גוי protects his own animal from becoming barren
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a גוי avoids bestiality with his own animal so it will not become barren.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא said in the name of רב שילא בר אבינא, quoting רב: A גוי takes care of his own animal so it will not become barren.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. A גוי would not do this to his own animal because it would hurt its ability to have young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bestiality can make an animal barren, and a barren animal is a loss to its owner. So the משנה's worry applies when the animal belongs to a Jew. When a גוי sells his own animal, he would have protected it.

phrases.english: Rav Taḥlifa said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא בַּר אֲבִינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Sheila bar Avina said in the name of Rav:
A gentile spares his own animal
so that it will not become barren.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁילָא בַּר אֲבִינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a גוי's own animal versus someone else's animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גוי is suspected of bestiality with any animal, even his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי holds back with his own animal to protect its fertility, so buying it from him is fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key idea for the rest of the passage: the suspicion depends on whose animal it is.

steps.title: What about male animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: barrenness only explains females, so why buy males?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for female animals. What can we say about males?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's answer. Males do not become barren, so the reason does not cover them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason only protects female animals. But the ברייתא allows buying any animal for a קרבן, and many קרבנות must be male. So we need a reason why a גוי would protect a male animal too.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for (one case), but what about the other?

phrases.english: This works well for females,
for males, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reason that a גוי protects his animal from barrenness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Males cannot become barren, so the reason does not explain why we may buy males.

steps.title: It weakens the flesh of male animals
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that bestiality weakens a male animal's body, so a גוי avoids it with males too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Because it weakens their flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a reason for males. Bestiality makes them physically weaker, so a גוי would protect them as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as before: a גוי does not want to damage his own property. For females the damage is barrenness, and for males it is a weaker, thinner body. So we may buy both from a גוי.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Since it weakens the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a parallel reason that covers the case left out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing stops a גוי from doing this with a male animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי protects males too, because it weakens their flesh.

steps.title: Buying from a גוי shepherd, whose animals are not his own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that allows buying from a גוי shepherd, who has no reason to protect animals that are not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what about what was taught in a ברייתא: We may buy an animal from their shepherd. Let us worry that he committed bestiality with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge. The 'he protects his own animal' reason does not work for a shepherd caring for someone else's animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 5 depend on the גוי being the owner. A shepherd loses nothing if someone else's animal becomes barren or weak. So this ברייתא seems to clash with the משנה again.

keyTerms.meaning: That which was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather, what about that which was taught:
We may buy an animal from their shepherd,
let us be concerned that perhaps he committed bestiality with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case where the answers of steps 3 and 5 do not help.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that a גוי protects his own animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shepherd does not own the animals, so he has no reason to protect them, and the משנה's suspicion should apply.

steps.title: The shepherd is afraid of losing his pay
steps.stepSummary: A גוי shepherd avoids bestiality because he fears losing his wages if he is caught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their shepherd is afraid, because he could lose his wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the shepherd has his own reason to hold back: if this were found out, he would lose his job and his pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the animals are not his, the shepherd has something to lose. Damaging the owner's flock puts his income at risk. So we may buy from him without worry.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's suspicion of bestiality applies when the גוי has nothing to lose. We may buy an animal for a קרבן from a גוי owner, because he protects his own property: females from barrenness and males from weakness. We may also buy from a גוי shepherd, because he fears losing his wages.

phrases.english: Their shepherd is afraid
because of losing his wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different personal reason for the shepherd to hold back.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A shepherd has no reason to protect animals that are not his.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shepherd fears losing his wages, so he holds back too.

steps.title: Why may we not hand an animal to a gentile shepherd?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא forbidding a Jew to give an animal to a גוי shepherd. But by the last answer, the shepherd should fear losing his wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, look at this ברייתא: 'We may not hand over an animal to their shepherd.' Why not? Let us say their shepherd is afraid of losing his wages!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the previous step. If a גוי shepherd is afraid of losing his wages, why does a ברייתא forbid giving him our animal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 we said a hired גוי shepherd stays away from bestiality because he fears losing his pay. If that fear works, a Jew should also be allowed to hand his animal to a גוי shepherd. Yet this ברייתא forbids it, which seems to contradict the fear idea.

keyTerms.meaning: hand over, entrust (an animal to someone's care)
let us say (the reasoning that should apply)

phrases.english: Rather, that which is taught in a ברייתא:
One may not hand over an animal
to their shepherd,
Let us say: their shepherd
is afraid because of losing his wages!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'fear of losing wages' answer from step 7 using a ברייתא that seems to ignore that fear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that a גוי shepherd avoids bestiality out of fear of losing his wages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the fear works, the ruling should allow handing an animal to a גוי shepherd. The ברייתא forbids it, so the fear does not seem to work.

steps.title: Gentiles fear each other, but not Jews
steps.stepSummary: A גוי shepherd fears other גוים, who know his habits and could catch him. He does not fear Jews, who don't know his ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: They (גוים), who know about each other, are afraid. We, who don't know about them, they are not afraid of.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the shepherd's fear only works when his employer is a fellow גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fear of losing his wages only matters if he thinks he could get caught. Another גוי understands his behavior and would notice, so he holds back. A Jew is not familiar with such behavior and would not suspect anything, so the fear is gone. That is why handing him a Jew's animal is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: they know about each other (each other's behavior)

phrases.english: They, who know about each other, are afraid.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן דְּלָא יָדְעִינַן בְּהוּ, לָא מִרַתְתִי.
phrases.english: We, who do not know about them, they are not afraid of.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 8 by limiting step 7's fear to an employer who is a גוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: who the owner is (a גוי or a Jew).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fear of losing wages should protect any animal given to a גוי shepherd, even a Jew's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fear only works when the owner is a fellow גוי who would know to suspect him. With a Jewish owner there is no fear, so handing him the animal is forbidden.

steps.title: רבה's saying: a sinner recognizes another sinner
steps.stepSummary: רבה backs up the answer with a popular saying: just as a stylus cuts into marble, a sinner can spot a fellow sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This is what people say: 'A stylus cuts into marble; a sinner knows his fellow.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a folk saying that supports the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer said גוים can catch one another but Jews cannot. רבה's saying explains why: people who do the same wrong things can see right through each other. Jews, who don't behave this way, would not pick up on it.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what people say (introduces a popular saying)
a stylus, a sharp writing tool
a sinner, someone used to doing wrong

phrases.english: רבה said:
This is what people say:
A stylus cuts into marble,
phrases.notes: The picture: something sharp cuts right through something hard. That is how one sinner sees right through another.

phrases.english: a sinner knows his fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9's distinction with a popular saying.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that גוים recognize each other's sins, while Jews do not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A folk saying quoted by רבה: 'A stylus cuts into marble; a sinner knows his fellow.'

steps.title: Then don't buy male animals from gentile women
steps.stepSummary: A gentile woman has no reason to fear harming a male animal by bestiality. So the גמרא asks: we should not buy male animals from women.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us not buy male animals from women, since we should worry that perhaps she had it mate with her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the idea that a גוי avoids bestiality to protect his own animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, a גוי holds back so his animal won't become barren or weak. When a woman sins with a male animal, the animal is not harmed that way, so that reason would not stop her. We should then worry about buying male animals from her, yet this is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (if your reasoning is right)
she has an animal mate with her

phrases.english: If so,
let us not buy male animals from women,
phrases.notes: Here נקבות means gentile women who own the animals, not female animals.

phrases.english: since we should worry that perhaps
she had it mate with her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, זְכָרִים מִנְּקֵבוֹת לָא נִיזְבּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the shepherd question is settled, the גמרא finds a case the 'protect your own animal' reason does not cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasons from steps 3 and 5: a גוי avoids bestiality to keep his animal from becoming barren or weak.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman with a male animal causes neither barrenness nor weakness, so nothing should hold her back. Buying males from women should then be forbidden.

steps.title: The animal would follow her and expose her
steps.stepSummary: A woman stays away from this sin because the animal would keep following her around in public, and people would find out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it would follow her around, she is afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a different fear holds the woman back: being exposed by the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about harming the animal does not apply here, but shame does. After such a sin, the male animal would trail after her where everyone could see. Fear of being found out keeps her away, so we may buy male animals from her.

keyTerms.meaning: it is drawn to her, follows her around

phrases.english: Since it would follow her around, she is afraid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 11 by giving a new reason for fear: being exposed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason: fear of being found out replaces fear of harming the animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the male animal is not harmed, nothing stops a woman from this sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal would follow her in public and expose her. That fear keeps her away, so buying male animals from women is allowed.

steps.title: Then why may a widow not raise a dog?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף taught that a widow should not raise a dog. But if a dog would follow her and expose her, she should be afraid to sin with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב יוסף taught: 'A widow should not raise a dog, and should not host a תורה student as a lodger.' The student makes sense, since he is discreet in her eyes. But a dog: since it would follow her, she is afraid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 12 with a teaching of רב יוסף. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about the student fits, because she trusts him to keep a secret, so nothing scares her off. But by step 12, a dog that follows her around would expose her, so she should be afraid and the rule should not be needed. The fact that רב יוסף forbids the dog seems to show that this fear does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: a תורה student (literally, 'son of the house of the רב')
lodging, staying as a guest in a home
granted, it makes sense (sets up the contrast)

steps.confusionAlert: The worry about the student is not that he is a known sinner. The point is that she sees him as discreet, so fear of being found out would not hold her back.

phrases.english: But what about what רב יוסף taught:
A widow should not raise a dog,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא תַּשְׁרֵי בַּר בֵּי רַב בְּאוּשְׁפִּיזָא.
phrases.english: and should not host a Torah student as a lodger.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בַּר בֵּי רַב צְנִיעַ לַהּ,
phrases.english: Granted, the student is discreet in her eyes,
but a dog,
since it would follow her, she is afraid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 12's 'the animal follows her' answer using רב יוסף's teaching about a widow and a dog.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that a woman fears an animal that would follow her and expose her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that fear works, a widow could safely raise a dog. רב יוסף forbids it, which suggests the fear is not enough.

steps.title: People would think the dog follows her because of meat
steps.stepSummary: A dog following a widow would not expose her, because people would think she fed it meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a dog also follows a woman when she throws it a piece of meat, people will say: it follows her because of the meat. So she has no reason to be afraid, and that is why a widow should not raise a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רב יוסף from Step 13. A dog following a woman does not make anyone suspicious, because dogs follow people who feed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said that an animal following a woman around would expose her, so she stays away from sin. A dog is different: dogs follow anyone who throws them food, so people have an innocent explanation ready. Since she has nothing to fear, רב יוסף's warning about a widow and a dog stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows after her, it trails her

phrases.english: Since when she throws it a piece of meat
it also follows after her,
people will say:
The fact that it follows after her
is because of the meat that it follows.
phrases.notes: So nobody would suspect her, and nothing stops her from sinning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from רב יוסף in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a dog has an innocent reason to follow her, so following does not expose her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dog following her would expose her just like any other animal, so she would be afraid.
steps.terutzMaskana: People would think the dog follows her for food, so she is not deterred, and רב יוסף's warning makes sense.

steps.title: Why not leave female animals with gentile women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why female animals may not be left alone with gentile women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Female animals with females: what is the reason we do not leave them alone together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and sets up the answers that come next. Since a gentile woman would not sin with a female animal, why is it forbidden to leave one with her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry so far was that the person watching the animal would sin with it. A woman with a female animal does not fit that worry. So the גמרא needs a different reason for the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We leave alone together (from יִחוּד, seclusion)

phrases.english: Females with females,
phrases.notes: Female animals left in the care of gentile women.

phrases.english: what is the reason we do not leave them alone together?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקֵבוֹת אֵצֶל נְקֵבוֹת, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מְיַיחֲדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the dog discussion is settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for forbidding a female animal to be left alone with a gentile woman.

steps.title: The visiting gentile man may find the animal instead
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא בר חמא explains that gentile men visit other men's wives, and if the wife isn't there, he may sin with the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא בר חמא said: Because gentiles often visit their friends' wives, and sometimes he doesn't find her, so he finds the animal and sins with it.
steps.whatsHappening: מר עוקבא בר חמא answers the question. The danger is not the woman. It is a gentile man who comes to visit her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry moves from the woman to a man who comes into her house. If she is not home, the animal is there, and he may sin with it. So the animal is not safe in her house either.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva bar Ḥama said:
Because gentiles are often found
with the wives of their friends,
and sometimes he does not find her,
and he finds the animal and sins with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A visiting gentile man who doesn't find the woman may sin with the animal instead.

steps.title: Even if he finds her, he still prefers the animal
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even when he finds the woman he may still sin with the animal, because gentiles find a Jew's animal more appealing than their own wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: even when he finds her, he also sins with the animal. As the Master said: a Jew's animal is more appealing to them than their own wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, stronger answer. The danger exists even when the woman is home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer needed the woman to be out. This answer says that doesn't matter, because they are drawn to a Jew's animal even more than to their wives. The next step explains where this desire comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
even when he finds her, he also sins with it,
as the Master said:
The animal of a Jew is more appealing to them
than their own wives,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 15 that is broader than Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is at risk even when the woman is home, since gentiles prefer a Jew's animal.

steps.title: The נחש left a spiritual dirtiness in חוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains: when the נחש came on חוה, it put זוהמא, a spiritual dirtiness, into her.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: When the snake came upon חוה, it put a dirtiness into her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן to explain where this strange desire comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זוהמא from the נחש passed down to all people. It is the source of these unnatural desires. This sets up the obvious question in the next step: wouldn't Jews have it too?

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
At the time the snake came upon Eve
it put a dirtiness into her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That gentiles have an unnatural desire for a Jew's animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement about the זוהמא the נחש put into חוה.

steps.title: Then Jews should have it too
steps.stepSummary: If the זוהמא came from חוה, Jews come from her too and should have it as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, Jews too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's idea. Everyone comes from חוה, including Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dirtiness passed to all of חוה's children, there is no reason it should only be in gentiles. Then Jews should be suspected too.

phrases.english: If so, Jews too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation that the זוהמא came from חוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All people come from חוה, so Jews should carry the זוהמא too.

steps.title: הר סיני removed the dirtiness from ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Jews who stood at הר סיני had their זוהמא stopped. Gentiles, who did not stand there, still have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Jews, who stood at הר סיני, their dirtiness ended. Gentiles, who did not stand at הר סיני, their dirtiness did not end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that receiving the תורה at הר סיני cleaned away the זוהמא for ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone started with the זוהמא. מתן תורה at הר סיני stopped it for the Jews, but not for those who weren't there. That is why only gentiles are suspected.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the תורה was given

steps.whatToRemember: The זוהמא from the נחש stayed in people until הר סיני. Standing there and receiving the תורה is what cleaned it from ישראל.

phrases.english: Jews, who stood at Mount Sinai —
their dirtiness ended,

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹיִם שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי —
phrases.english: gentiles, who did not stand at Mount Sinai —
their dirtiness did not end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: an event (הר סיני) that changed ישראל but not the gentiles.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since all come from חוה, all should carry the זוהמא equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זוהמא ended for ישראל at הר סיני, but remains in gentiles.

steps.title: What about birds?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether gentiles are suspected of this sin with birds too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law with birds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question and sets up the proofs that follow. Does the worry about animals also include birds?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about animals like cattle and sheep. Birds are much smaller, so maybe the concern does not apply. The question is whether one may leave birds with a gentile.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Birds, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question after the topic of female animals ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether gentiles are suspected of bestiality with birds.

steps.title: רבי חנינא saw a gentile do this with a goose
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא testified that he saw a gentile buy a goose, sin with it, strangle it, roast it and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, in the name of רבי חנינא: I saw a gentile who bought a goose in the market, sinned with it, strangled it, roasted it, and ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an eyewitness story to answer the question. It shows that gentiles are suspected with birds as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question about birds is answered with a real case someone saw. If it happened even with a goose, birds are included in the worry.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina:
I saw a gentile
who bought a goose from the market,
sinned with it, strangled it, roasted it, and ate it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21 with an eyewitness report.
steps.raayaObject: That gentiles are suspected of bestiality with birds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's eyewitness account of a gentile and a goose.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה saw an Arab do this with a piece of meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה מדיפתי adds a second story: an Arab carved out a piece of meat, sinned with it, roasted it and ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה מדיפתי said: I saw an Arab who bought a thigh in the market, carved a hole in it big enough to sin with, sinned with it, roasted it, and ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second eyewitness story. It shows how far this behavior could go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone would even do this with a piece of dead meat, he would surely do it with a live bird. This makes the proof from the goose even stronger.
steps.whatToRemember: Birds are included in the worry. Two eyewitness stories (a goose, and even a piece of meat) show that gentiles were suspected with them.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said:
I saw a certain Arab
who bought a thigh from the market,
and carved into it enough for the act,
sinned with it, roasted it, and ate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger eyewitness story to the proof of Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That gentiles are suspected with birds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ירמיה מדיפתי's eyewitness account involving a piece of meat.
